headline: Blackwell-driven surge lifts revenue and margins sharply
summary_short: NVIDIA's fiscal Q1 2027 revenue surged to $81.62B (+85.2% y/y, +20.0% q/q) on Data Center/Blackwell demand, while net income more than tripled to $58.32B as gross margin rebounded to 74.9% from 60.5% a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 85% y/y and 20% q/q to $81.62B, led by Data Center ($75.2B, +92% y/y) on the Blackwell 300 ramp and InfiniBand/Spectrum-X/NVLink demand; Edge Computing added $6.4B (+29% y/y). Gross margin expanded to 74.9% from 60.5% a year ago, mainly because last year included a $4.5B H20 inventory charge that didn't recur; sequentially flat. Opex rose 52% y/y and 12% q/q on compensation, compute/infrastructure, and engineering-development costs. Net income more than tripled y/y to $58.32B, boosted by a $16.1B swing in other income from unrealized equity gains; effective tax rate rose to 16.6% from 14.3%. NVIDIA repurchased $20.2B of stock, paid $243M dividends; cash plus marketable securities: $50.3B.

drivers.explanation: Data Center demand for AI/accelerated computing drove the increase (+92% y/y); Blackwell architecture remained the majority of shipments. No H20 shipments to China this quarter vs $4.6B a year ago.
Non-recurrence of the prior-year $4.5B H20 excess-inventory and purchase-obligation charge lifted gross margin to 74.9% from 60.5%; margin was roughly flat sequentially.
Revenue growth outpaced a 52% y/y rise in operating expenses; Compute & Networking segment operating income also benefited from the non-recurrence of last year's H20 charge.
Boosted by a $16.1B favorable swing in other income, driven by unrealized gains of $13.4B on publicly-held equity securities and $2.6B on non-marketable equity securities.
Effective tax rate rose to 16.6% from 14.3% because stock-based-compensation tax benefits were a smaller share of a much larger pretax income base.
